NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Platform / Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior platform and site reliability engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including the last 6 years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in designing, building and operating cloud infrastructure, maintaining Terraform-based environments, and supporting product teams with reliable, observable platforms. Tech lead for a five-person platform team, with a track record of leading technical work across teams and delivering measurable improvements in deployment speed, reliability and cloud cost.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Linux
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane, Puppet
Platform engineering: Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Karpenter, GitHub Actions
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Automation and testing: Go, Python, Bash, k6

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 – Present
- Tech lead for a five-person platform team operating an AWS EKS platform across 8 clusters and 3 regions, supporting approximately 350 services.
- Built an internal developer platform with golden-path service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3. Adopted by all 14 product teams, it reduced the time from new service to production from around two weeks to under one day.
- Led Terraform-based provisioning of platform capabilities and supported teams in deploying services that are easier to operate.
- Introduced SLOs and burn-rate alerts for the 20 most critical services, with an error-budget policy agreed with product leadership; on-call pages per week fell by approximately 60%.
- Replaced cluster-autoscaler managed node groups with Karpenter and introduced spot instances for stateless workloads, reducing EC2 spend by 38% (approximately GBP 410,000 per year).
- Serve in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game-backend infrastructure (EC2, ECS and later EKS) for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure with Terraform across approximately 40 modules, using Atlantis for plan and apply workflows on pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Planned capacity and ran k6 load tests ahead of launches. A 2020 test simulating 300,000 concurrent players identified a connection-pool limit that was fixed before launch.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Sheffield | Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and participated in on-call customer incident response.

SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes cleanup controller | Open source side project | 2024
- Built a small Go controller using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; the project has approximately 120 GitHub stars.

LEADERSHIP & COMMUNITY
- Mentored three engineers moving from backend engineering into SRE.
- Speaker at a UK DevOps meetup in 2024: “SLOs that product managers care about”.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, polished CV with clear progression from Linux systems engineering to senior platform leadership. The structure is logical, the summary is targeted, and the experience bullets use credible scale and measurable outcomes: 8 clusters, 350 services, 14 product teams, 60% fewer pages, and £410,000 annual savings. The document also demonstrates technical leadership without falsely implying line management. The selected project, speaking engagement, mentoring, certifications, and relevant education add useful evidence. Minor content limitations are that systems architecture, networking, security, and stakeholder alignment are not described as explicitly as the target role requires. These are partly genuine experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is very good. Standard section headings, chronological experience, plain text formatting, recognizable technology names, and clear role/company/date formatting should parse reliably. Relevant terms such as AWS, EKS, Terraform, Kubernetes, Linux, VPC, IAM, RDS, SQS, observability, incident management, and technical lead are present. The CV also has a strong likelihood of passing general AI screening for AWS platform, SRE, Kubernetes, and Terraform roles because the claims are specific and quantified. Screening probability for this particular role is somewhat reduced by the absence of Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, explicit system design terminology, and explicit security/networking achievements. These are not document defects where the original candidate information does not support the experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV strongly demonstrates hands-on infrastructure engineering and AWS cloud environment operation through EKS, EC2, ECS, Terraform, Kubernetes, Linux, and large-scale production platforms. Terraform, technical leadership, analytical thinking, communication, reliability, and support for backend/product teams are well evidenced. AWS, Linux, and virtual-machine-related experience are shown. The internal developer platform and golden-path work aligns particularly well with helping backend developers deploy services that are easy to monitor and operate. The CV does not show Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS implementation, certificate management, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, or JVM/full-stack experience; these are candidate-material gaps, not defects that can be solved by wording. Practical security awareness is only lightly evidenced through IAM and should be made more explicit if the existing AWS/IAM work included concrete security responsibilities. The culture fit is credible through ownership of platforms, technical leadership, mentoring, cross-team enablement, and a 2024 technical talk, although the CV appropriately avoids unsupported claims about Corvale's culture.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ALIGNMENT ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, change the sentence beginning "Experienced in designing, building and operating cloud infrastructure" to explicitly include system design and cross-team technical leadership, using only the experience already shown. For example: "Experienced in designing, building and operating AWS cloud infrastructure and Kubernetes platforms, shaping platform architecture, and leading technical work across product teams."
2. In the Senior Platform Engineer section under Tallybrook Ltd, revise the first bullet to make the architecture scope clearer: "Tech lead for a five-person platform team designing and operating an AWS EKS platform across 8 clusters and 3 regions, supporting approximately 350 services." This uses the existing platform scale and leadership evidence while aligning more directly with "cloud environment design and operation."
3. In the same Tallybrook section, revise the internal developer platform bullet to state the stakeholder and interface dimension already supported by the evidence: "Built and led adoption of an internal developer platform with golden-path service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3; adopted by all 14 product teams and reduced time from new service to production from around two weeks to under one day." This more clearly demonstrates leading a technical topic and bringing product teams along.
4. In the Core Skills section, change the existing "Cloud infrastructure" line to "Cloud infrastructure and networking: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Linux". Do not add mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, or Terragrunt, because those are not supported by the original candidate information.
5. If the listed AWS IAM and VPC experience involved concrete security or network-design responsibilities, add one truthful, specific phrase to the relevant Tallybrook or Brightwater bullet—for example, the actual IAM, VPC, access-control, or network-segmentation responsibility performed. Do not add a generic claim such as "security-aware" without an example; the original information currently supports only the presence of IAM/VPC in the skills list.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, polished CV with a clear senior platform-engineering profile, relevant scale, strong quantified outcomes, and credible leadership evidence. The experience bullets are concise and outcome-focused: platform adoption, deployment-time reduction, reliability improvement, and cloud-cost reduction are especially persuasive. The structure is professional and easy to scan. The main content limitation is that the CV is optimized for general platform/SRE roles rather than this specific fleet-connectivity engagement: systems architecture, networking, security, and stakeholder-facing technical proposal work are not described explicitly enough. Removing the Pennine Hosting role follows the candidate's instruction, although it means the stated 10 years of experience is not fully visible in the employment timeline.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, standard chronological experience, plain text contact details, recognizable technology names, and no problematic tables, graphics, columns, or decorative formatting. AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, Linux, observability, incident management, and technical leadership keywords are prominent. AI screening probability is high for AWS/platform/SRE roles, approximately 88–92%. Matching is weaker for this particular advert because Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, system design, and fleet/remote-device integration are not present. Terragrunt and mTLS/TLS should not be added because they are not supported by the original candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document strongly demonstrates hands-on infrastructure engineering and AWS cloud operation through EKS, EC2, Terraform, VPC, IAM, and multi-region production platforms. It also shows technical leadership, stakeholder alignment, analytical thinking, and communication through the five-person team lead role, the error-budget policy agreed with product leadership, measurable operational improvements, mentoring, and the meetup presentation. Terraform is clearly demonstrated, but Terragrunt is not supported by the candidate's material. The CV shows relevant Linux and virtual-machine/cloud-compute experience through Linux and EC2. Systems architecture and system design are reasonably evidenced by the internal developer platform and platform-capability work, but could be stated more directly. Practical security awareness is only lightly evidenced through IAM and network-related AWS services. Networking specifically involving mTLS, SSL/TLS, or certificate management is a gap, as are IoT, automotive, and remote-device integration. A JVM backend/full-stack background is also a gap; the candidate's supported programming experience is Go, Python, and Bash. The leadership and ownership examples fit Corvale's engineering-led, collaborative, fast-moving culture, although the CV could make cross-team technical influence more explicit.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, change the sentence beginning "Experienced in designing, building and operating cloud infrastructure" to explicitly include systems architecture and technical stakeholder leadership, using only supported evidence. For example: "Experienced in designing, building and operating AWS cloud infrastructure and internal developer platforms, leading technical work across teams, and agreeing reliability practices with product leadership."
2. In the Senior Platform Engineer experience section, revise "Led Terraform-based provisioning of platform capabilities and supported teams in deploying services that are easier to operate" to make the system-design and developer-enablement contribution more concrete: "Led Terraform-based provisioning of platform capabilities and supported 14 product teams in designing and deploying services with consistent operational defaults and observability." This is supported by the internal developer platform and its adoption by all 14 product teams.
3. In the Senior Platform Engineer experience section, strengthen the existing VPC/IAM/security signal without adding unsupported security claims. Add the supported AWS services to the Terraform/platform bullet where accurate, for example: "Led Terraform-based provisioning of AWS platform capabilities across VPC, IAM, RDS, SQS and S3." Only use this wording if those services were part of the provisioning work described in the original candidate information; otherwise retain the current wording and rely on the AWS skills line.
4. In the Core Skills section, retain "AWS ... VPC, IAM" and "Linux" but do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT, automotive, JVM, Istio, Linkerd, or unsupported security tools. These are unsupported gaps rather than CV wording problems.
